answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: The liquid cooling supports the 99.9% availability target with concurrently maintainable CDUs (redundant pumps, isolation valves and N+1 units per group), and is designed for 45 °C facility water and the stated design ambient in the mechanical galleries. Our CDUs are indoor equipment, so the outdoor ratings do not apply to them, and seismic category D anchoring is still to be confirmed.
answers.reason: Block redundancy for power (DB-07) and the outdoor ratings (DB-10) are outside the cooling scope; seismic category D bracing of the CDU frames has not yet been qualified for this site.
answers.next_steps: Complete a seismic anchoring assessment of the CDU frames with the structural engineer.

Illustrative placeholder response: The liquid cooling is designed for warm facility water up to 45 °C on the CDU primary side, and we will state the maximum water inlet and expected outlet temperatures for the final rack configuration in the cooling data table.
answers.conditions: Temperatures depend on the final GPU heat load per rack, fixed at the technical decision point.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We offer modular liquid-to-liquid row CDUs in the mechanical galleries with N+1 redundancy per group, taking facility water on the primary side and serving a separate technical-grade secondary loop to the GPU cold plates at 1.5 LPM per kW or more. With the CDUs we offer JetCool direct-to-chip cold plates for the GPUs, sized to the rack design; their thermal ratings are stated in the tender data sheets once the accelerator is fixed. The CDU data sheet will give rated kW, pump type and count, temperatures, secondary flow, available lift, filter mesh, pipe routing and power supply.
answers.next_steps: Size the CDU groups per hall once the rack layout is shared.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: For auxiliary racks above 20 kW we offer liquid-assisted air cooling that removes most of the heat without facility water, and our cooling equipment operates with ASHRAE A2 supply air. Operation at A3 is not yet confirmed for every auxiliary configuration.
answers.reason: A3 operation depends on the auxiliary IT equipment's own rating and has not been qualified with our liquid-assisted modules for this configuration.
answers.next_steps: Qualify A3 operation with the compute supplier during the dialogue.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We will state the thermal ride-through at full load and the automatic restart sequence of the CDUs. For a dependable ride-through we propose powering the CDU pumps and controls from the UPS-backed supply rather than relying on loop thermal mass alone.
answers.reason: With loop thermal mass alone, ride-through at full GPU load may be shorter than the time backup generation needs to restart the plant, which risks GPU throttling or shutdown.
answers.workaround: Feed the CDU pumps and controls (a small share of the cooling load) from the UPS-backed bus and add a buffer volume on the secondary loop, so coolant keeps circulating until generation restarts the plant.
answers.next_steps: Confirm the UPS capacity for the pump load with the power team.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We will deliver a chemical management plan for the secondary loop coolant, covering additives, water properties, transport, storage, filling, draining and disposal, nine months before delivery.

Illustrative placeholder response: Each CDU measures flow, temperature and pressure per loop, with sampling frequency, accuracy and timestamps stated, and we will give piping routes and CDU floor loading for each hall. Per-node measurement needs sensors at the rack manifold or in the node, which are not part of our standard offer.
answers.reason: Per-node cooling measurement and rack weight depend on the compute racks and node telemetry supplied by the compute team; our standard CDU offer measures per loop.
answers.next_steps: Agree with the compute team whether node-level flow and temperature come from the node or from instrumented manifolds.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We offer five years of 24 by 7 maintenance and support from acceptance, with a four-hour response, concurrent maintenance of the CDUs and an on-site parts cache. We propose that the 2-hour repair target means restoring full cooling, which the redundant pumps and hot-swappable modules give, with the permanent repair completed within 6 hours.
answers.reason: A full component repair within 2 hours at any hour would need resident cooling technicians on site 24 by 7 for five years, which adds cost without improving cooling availability.
answers.workaround: The 2-hour target covers restoring full cooling (automatic failover to the redundant pump or CDU, or a hot-swap by trained staff), and the permanent repair follows within 6 hours.
answers.next_steps: Discuss the repair-time definition in the dialogue sessions.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our prices are in US dollars, free of taxes, and cover delivery to site, installation, commissioning and training, with the price schedule separating equipment, freight, installation, commissioning, spares and five years of maintenance, and any extension priced as an option. We propose a metals price adjustment for phases delivered more than 18 months after award, listed in the commercial exceptions schedule.
answers.reason: Copper and stainless steel are a large share of CDU and manifold cost, and a fully firm price for phases delivered two or more years out would carry a large risk premium.
answers.workaround: Prices are firm for deliveries within 18 months of award; later phases are adjusted by a published metals index with a stated cap, or the Owner may choose a firm price that includes a stated risk premium.
answers.next_steps: Bid manager to confirm the exception does not make the bid non-responsive under CT-03 and CT-08.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our cooling prices are unconditional, with no 'to be discussed' items or references to separate contracts; any exception appears only in the separate commercial exceptions schedule.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We accept liquidated damages for missed service levels, capped by the at-risk amounts described, and delay penalties that scale with the length of the delay and the seriousness of the breach, subject to an aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together.
answers.reason: Liquidated damages and delay penalties have no overall limit as written, which leaves an open-ended risk on a phased multi-lot delivery.
answers.workaround: An aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together, set as a percentage of each lot's price; the percentage is stated in the financial offer and listed in the commercial exceptions schedule (CT-08).

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our commercial exceptions are listed in the separate exceptions schedule and kept to a minimum: on liquidated damages, only the aggregate cap per lot asked for under CT-07; any indexed price is shown there only as an alternative to the firm price.

Illustrative placeholder response: Warranty for the cooling equipment is included in the five-year maintenance period, and we take responsibility for failures caused by disturbances foreseeable within the Section 9 interface limits.

Illustrative placeholder response: We provide a supply-chain security and risk plan for the cooling components, with named second sources for pumps, sensors and controllers. Instead of a guarantee for each original component over the system's whole lifetime, we commit to the availability period stated as the proposed change.
answers.reason: No supplier can guarantee every original component for an open-ended system lifetime: electronic parts follow their makers' life cycles.
answers.workaround: Spare parts or compatible form-fit-function replacements available for at least 10 years from acceptance, with at least 12 months' notice of end of life and a last-time-buy offer before any component is discontinued.
